$comment: The controller-result contract, in one document, read mechanically by
every side of it.
The consumer is Go: internal/unattended/controller.go decides what a run
does next from a supervised task's own statement of what happened. A
producer is anything that writes that statement, and there are two. On the
Windows host this engine's pilot runs on it is PowerShell,
corsolv/powershell/CorsolvControllerResult.psm1. On the delivery host it is
the Bash driver, corsolv/delivery/controller-contract.sh.
Neither producer decides anything. There is no disposition, no retry
policy and no gate verdict on the producing side, because all three are
the run's to decide, and a second opinion in a second language is a second
authority that can disagree.
Implementations of one wire format drift. This file is what stops them:
internal/unattended/controller_contract_test.go asserts the Go vocabulary
and adjudication match it; corsolv/powershell/CorsolvControllerResult.Tests.ps1
asserts the module emits and validates exactly these documents; and
corsolv/delivery/driver_parity_test.go writes every fixture below through
the Bash producer and adjudicates it with the real Go consumer. No
implementation is the authority; this file is, and all three are checked
against it.
